summary: Phase 3.6 Orion analytics interceptor — 30/31 backend tests PASS. Founder/admin analytics intents bypass OpenAI and return deterministic markdown (3-9ms p95), non-admin refusal works without leaking permission errors (HTTP 200 with polite refusal + model='orion-analytics'), audit log captures every attempt including 'refused: not_admin', non-analytics messages still fall through to gpt-4o-mini, read-only invariant verified by static check (the ONLY write call in orion_analytics.py is to orion_admin_query_logs). 1 ROUTING BUG found: 'How many users signed up this week?' incorrectly routes to total_users intent instead of signups.

minor.issue: The phrase 'How many users signed up this week?' (explicitly listed in the review request) routes to the `total_users` tool instead of `signups`. Root cause: the `signups` regex `\b(sign[\s-]?ups|new\s+users|registrations|new\s+sign[\s-]?ups)\b` does NOT match the past-tense verb form 'signed up' / 'signed-up'. Since signups misses, the next pattern `total_users` (`how\s+many\s+users`) matches and returns just the total user count instead of the today/week/total breakdown. Fix: extend the signups regex to include `signed[\s-]?up(s)?` (e.g. `\b(sign[\s-]?ups?|signed[\s-]?up|new\s+users|registrations)\b`), OR tighten total_users so it doesn't fire when 'signed up' follows. Verified by direct call: `detect_intent('How many users signed up this week?')` -> 'total_users'.

tests_executed.TestFounderAnalytics: 8/9 PASS — today_snapshot, investor_snapshot, dau, top_realms, support, moderation, badges, widgets all return model='orion-analytics' with the required markdown headers. FAIL: 'How many users signed up this week?' (see minor issue above).
tests_executed.TestIntentRouter: 9/9 PASS — DAU?, weekly active users, how many users total?, sounds uploaded today, top creators, new realms this week, moderation queue, open tickets, vip holders all route to model='orion-analytics'.
tests_executed.TestFallThrough: 2/2 PASS — 'Hello there' (founder) and 320-char garbage non-keyword (founder) both fall through to gpt-4o-mini, NOT orion-analytics.
tests_executed.TestRefusalPath: 2/2 PASS — tfone on the public iter62_orion_test widget gets exact refusal string + model='orion-analytics' + HTTP 200 (no 4xx); subsequent normal chat falls through to gpt-4o-mini.
tests_executed.TestEdgeCases: 1/1 PASS — empty message returns 422 from pydantic min_length=1.
tests_executed.TestPerformance: 1/1 PASS — 5 sequential 'today snapshot' calls all complete in <2s (observed 3-9ms per call).
tests_executed.TestAuditLog: 1/1 PASS — orion_admin_query_logs row for founder has all required fields (user_id, username, role, question, detected_intent, tool_called, timestamp, success, execution_time_ms, short_result_summary); non-admin refusal row has success=false and short_result_summary='refused: not_admin'; verified no 'Bearer' or 'api_key' substrings in the persisted question.
tests_executed.TestReadOnly: 1/1 PASS — static scan of orion_analytics.py for {insert,update,delete,replace}_one/many proves every write is on the orion_admin_query_logs collection. Zero writes to users/posts/realms/badges/widgets.

action_items: FIX intent router so 'How many users signed up this week?' resolves to signups. Suggested patch in /app/backend/services/orion_analytics.py line ~40 — change the signups regex to `\b(sign[\s-]?ups?|signed[\s-]?up|new\s+users|registrations|new\s+sign[\s-]?ups)\b` (adds the past-tense form). Alternatively, put a more specific signups-intent guard ahead of total_users that checks for 'signed' or 'this week' tokens. Add a regression test case in test_phase36_orion_analytics.py once fixed.
critical_code_review_comments: Intent ordering relies on first-match-wins. The total_users regex `how\s+many\s+users` is broad — consider negative lookahead like `(?!.*sign(ed|ups?))` to prevent accidental capture of signup questions. This was the root cause of the only failing test.
_role_for() hardcodes username 'stealth' -> 'founder'. If/when founder username changes this becomes wrong — consider reading from current.get('admin_role') or current.get('is_founder') first.

_safe_count() calls db.list_collection_names() on EVERY count — this issues an extra Mongo round-trip per metric. For tools like _tool_today_snapshot() that need 6 counts, this is ~6 list calls. Cache the collection list once per request (e.g. pass it into the tool fns) — would improve the 9ms hot path further.

_tool_top_realms() label fallback uses `a['_id'] or 'unknown'` — but `_id` is the grouped realm_id field, fine. Just confirm community_messages docs always carry `realm_id` not `community_id` (some legacy collections use the latter).
Audit-log try/except swallows ALL exceptions silently (line 451). Consider logger.exception() inside so ops can spot Mongo issues — currently audit-log failures are completely invisible.

maybe_handle_admin_query is correctly placed BEFORE _check_chat_rate in widget_chat.py line 175, so analytics calls don't consume rate-limit budget — confirmed by spec and verified by 5 sequential calls all 200 OK.
seed_data_creation: Created and cleaned up widget_registry doc {key:'iter62_orion_test', founder_only:false} for the refusal path via pymongo (auto-cleanup in module-scoped fixture teardown). No DB pollution. The orion_admin_query_logs collection now has 56 rows (4 pre-existing smoke + 52 from this test run, all under the ~30 budget per test class, distributed across 31 tests with parametrized variants).
context_for_next_testing_agent: Phase 3.6 Orion analytics is functionally working. Only outstanding issue is the signups intent regex missing the 'signed up' verb form — a one-line fix. /app/backend/tests/test_phase36_orion_analytics.py is the regression suite — uses pymongo (sync) for any direct DB checks because motor doesn't survive multiple asyncio.run() calls across tests. Existing iter62_orion_test widget is cleaned up automatically; if a previous run aborted, db.widget_registry.delete_many({key:'iter62_orion_test'}) is safe to run.
rca of the issue: RCA for failing intent: INTENTS list in services/orion_analytics.py iterates with first-match-wins. Order is [investor_snapshot, today_snapshot, dau, wau, mau, signups, total_users, ...]. For 'How many users signed up this week?': signups regex `\b(sign[\s-]?ups|new\s+users|registrations|new\s+sign[\s-]?ups)\b` only matches the noun 'signups' or 'sign ups' / 'sign-ups', NOT the past-tense verb 'signed up'. Loop falls through to total_users `\b(...|how\s+many\s+users)\b` which matches 'How many users'. Reproduction (verified): set -a && . /app/backend/.env && python -c 'from services.orion_analytics import detect_intent; print(detect_intent("How many users signed up this week?"))' -> 'total_users'. Mitigation: extend signups regex to include `signed[\s-]?up(s)?` so it wins before total_users, OR negative-lookahead in total_users.
